title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR — personal non-Adamic corruption not descending
pass_a_gloss: GAR asks: when God does not let each man's personal, adventitious corruption from his own actual sins descend to posterity—unlike the native Adamic corruption—is that acting against nature's order, overturning propagation laws, or blocking actual sin's natural sequel? He doubts anyone has said or even thought so.
pass_b_english: GAR. But when God does not permit the personal corruption of all men to descend into posterity—corruption, I say, not native and naturally implanted in all from Adam, but adventitious and sprouting from actual sins—is he to be thought to act against the order of nature, or to overturn the laws of natural propagation, or to hinder the natural sequel of actual sin? I can scarcely think this has hitherto been said by anyone, or even thought.
source_text: GAR. An vero, cum Deus corruptionem personalem omnium hominum non permittat in posteros descendere, corruptionem, inquam, non nativam ex Adamo naturaliter omnibus insitam, sed ascititiam, & ex actualibus peccatis progerminantem, putandus est contra naturae ordinem agere, aut leges naturalis propagationis evertere, aut peccati actualis naturalem sequelam impedire? Vix dictum putem hactenus a quoquam, aut cogitatum.

choices.choice: GAR: not letting personal sins' corruption descend ≠ against nature

notes: Cap. VI tertio densify section 361 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 259 tip–260 tip).
